map.Lessons 2-3, 2-4 & 2-5 — median, box plo: Lessons 2-3, 2-4 & 2-5 — median, box plots, range & IQR. Rosa has a hearing. Four gates stand in her way.
map.Previously: the reader proved Pimm's cen: Last time: the reader showed Pimm's census questions told us nothing. The glitch is still growing.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: the crew tore: Last time, in Episode 1: the crew took apart the "census form". The council saw. Now Rosa's hearing has a date.
map.Friday. That's how long we have to show: Friday is the day. The council must see Rosa's REAL counts.
map.Pimm keeps waving one terrible Tuesday a: Pimm keeps showing one bad Tuesday. One day is not my stall!
map.Then we don't show them one day. We show: Then we do not show one day. We show the middle of all her days. Her data sits around it.
map.The median is the middle value when the: The median is the middle value. The data must be in order. Half the days are at or below it. Half are at or above it.
map.Rosa's notebook. Five market days, five: Rosa's book. Five days at the market. Five crowd counts.
map.Raw loot log. But it's shuffled — a midd: This list is mixed up. It must be sorted first. Then find the middle.
map.Sorting protocol: line the counts up sma: Put the counts in order, small to big. THEN find the middle one. It is spot three of five. That is the median. No adding.
map.Reader — sort Rosa's five days and find: Reader, sort Rosa's five days. Find her true middle!
map.Rosa's five market days: 22, 17, 30, 25,: Rosa's five market days: 22, 17, 30, 25, 19 people. Sort them in your head or on paper. Then type the median.
map.Conceptual: the median is the middle of: Conceptual: the median is the middle of the SORTED list. Half the days are below it. Half are above it. You must sort first.
Procedural: put them in order: 17, 19, ?, ?, ?. With five values, the median is the 3rd.
map.If the council won't read a table, they': The council will not read a table. So they get a BANNER. One box. Five numbers. No lies.
map.It's a box plot. Five numbers tell the w: It is a box plot. It uses five numbers. They are minimum, quartile 1, median, quartile 3, maximum. The box holds the middle half of the data.
map.Q1 is the median of the lower half; Q3 i: Q1 is the median of the low half. Q3 is the median of the top half. The box goes from Q1 to Q3.
map.Paint the three missing marks on the ban: Paint the three missing marks on the banner: Q1, median, Q3!
map.The co-op's seven recorded crowds, alrea: The co-op has seven crowd counts. They are in order: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20. The whiskers are done (min 4, max 20). Type the three missing marks.
map.Conceptual: the median splits the sorted: Conceptual: the median cuts the sorted list in half. Q1 is the median of the LOWER half. Q3 is the median of the UPPER half.
map.Procedural: 7 values → median is the 4th: Procedural: 7 values → the median is the 4th. Lower half is 4, 7, 9 (middle: ?). Upper half is 13, 16, 20 (middle: ?).
He is using the range: max minus min. Just two numbers. The two most odd ones.
map.Counter-protocol: the IQR — Q3 minus Q1: Our answer is the IQR: Q3 minus Q1. It shows the spread of the middle half. Outliers do not change it. It is the honest width.
map.Range = max − min (fragile). IQR = Q3 −: Range = max − min (weak). IQR = Q3 − Q1 (strong). Same data. Two very different stories.
map.Compute both widths, reader. Let's see w: Find both widths, reader. Which one does Pimm hide behind?
map.Same data: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20 (Q1 =: Same data: 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 16, 20 (Q1 = 7, Q3 = 16). Pimm uses one width. The crew uses the other. Find both.
map.Conceptual: range uses the two END value: Conceptual: range uses the two END values. Those are the most odd days. IQR uses the box edges. That is the calm middle half.
Procedural: Range = max − min = 20 − 4. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 16 − 7.
map.Thursday night. A new poster appears on: Thursday night. A new poster is on the council board. It has four numbers. It has no middle.
map.Ha! He thinks an even count breaks the m: Ha! He thinks an even count breaks the median. Boss fight!
map.When two values share the middle, the me: Two values may share the middle. Then the median is halfway between them. Add the two middles. Split the sum in half. That is the middle of it all.
map.Tomorrow we hand the council the middle: Tonight we crack Pimm's even-count puzzle. Then we show them the middle AND the width.
map.Reader takes this one. Banner's already: Reader takes this one. The banner is done. Do not make me paint it again.
map.Boss Gate: find the median of an even-co: Boss Gate: find the median of an even-count data set. Then say what a small IQR shows.
map.BOSS GATE. Two locks. Pimm's \"no median: BOSS GATE. Two locks. Pimm's "no median" claim ends here.
map.Pimm's \"audit\" lists four days: 8, 10,: Pimm's "audit" lists four days: 8, 10, 14, 18. He says an even count has NO median. Two locks:
map.Rosa's box plot shows a small IQR huggin: Rosa's box plot has a small IQR. It is close to her median. At the hearing, that PROVES:
map.Conceptual: with an even count, TWO valu: Conceptual: with an even count, TWO values share the middle. The median is halfway between them. Add them. Then split in half.
map.Procedural: the two middles of 8, 10, 14: Procedural: the two middles of 8, 10, 14, 18 are 10 and 14. Halfway between: (10 + 14) ÷ 2.
map.Median 22, box snug around the middle… m: Median 22. The box is tight around the middle. My stall looks as steady as it feels.
map.Friday: payout day. Pimm \"rounds\" ever: Friday is pay day. Pimm "rounds" each share. Guess who checks his division?
map.Median.Sort first. The middle value of a: Median.Sort first. With an odd count, it is the middle number. For even counts, go halfway between the two middles.
map.Box plot.Five numbers — min, Q1, median,: Box plot.Five numbers: min, Q1, median, Q3, max. The box holds the middle half of the data.
map.Range.Max minus min. Easy to compute, ea: Range.Max minus min. Easy to find. One odd day can break it.
IQR.Q3 minus Q1, the width of the box. Outliers can't move it.
map.\"Anyone can shout the loudest number. T: "Anyone can shout the biggest number. The middle speaks soft. It is most often right." — A.V.

map.17, 19, 22, 25, 30 — the middle is 22. R: 17, 19, 22, 25, 30. The middle is 22. That is Rosa's usual day.
map.30 is the middle of the UNSORTED list. S: 30 is the middle of the UNSORTED list. Sort first. Order changes it all.
map.Line the five counts up smallest to larg: Put the five counts in order, small to big. Then take the one in spot three.
map.Box from 7 to 16, line at 11 — the banne: Box from 7 to 16, line at 11. The banner is done. It shows the middle half.
map.Split the sorted list: median is the 4th: Split the sorted list. The median is the 4th of 7. Then take the middle of each half.
map.Range 16 — but IQR only 9. Pimm quoted t: Range 16, but IQR only 9. Pimm used the noise. The box tells the calm truth.

map.Lock 2 holds. A small IQR says the middl: Lock 2 is shut. Say the IQR is small. Then the middle half of days is CLOSE TOGETHER. What does that mean for Rosa?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Median 12 — even counts: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Median 12. Even counts can't hide. A tight box means steady crowds. See you at the hearing, Pimm.
